*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: docs/architecture.md
@@
 # Client configuration
 
-The client uses a 10 second timeout.
+The client uses a 30-second timeout. This is the current policy, enforced by the client configuration and its timeout contract test.
+
+The earlier 10-second timeout is historical and is no longer active.
*** Add File: docs/decisions/timeout-policy.md
+# Timeout policy migration
+
+Date: 2026-09-23
+
+## Problem
+
+The client configuration and its test already enforce a 30-second timeout, but the architecture page still described a 10-second timeout. This left the user-facing policy inconsistent with the implementation.
+
+## Decision
+
+The client timeout policy is 30 seconds. The architecture page now identifies 30 seconds as current and explicitly labels 10 seconds as the superseded historical policy. The implementation and test remain unchanged because both already match the current policy.
+
+## Alternatives considered
+
+- Change the implementation and test back to 10 seconds to match the stale documentation. Rejected because the current client behavior is already 30 seconds and the requested migration is to document that as policy.
+- Remove all mention of the former 10-second timeout. Rejected because preserving the historical context makes the documentation discrepancy and migration understandable without suggesting that 10 seconds remains active.
+
+## Consequences
+
+Current architecture documentation, implementation, and test agree on 30 seconds. The prior 10-second policy remains documented only as historical context.
*** End Patch
'@ | apply_patch"

# Client timeout policy

## Problem

The architecture page described a 10-second client timeout even though the implementation and contract test use 30 seconds. This left the documented policy ambiguous and stale.

## Alternatives considered

- Keep 10 seconds as the active documented value, which would contradict the implementation and test.
- Remove the historical 10-second value entirely, losing context about the former policy.
- Document 30 seconds as current and retain 10 seconds only as migration history.

## Decision

The client timeout is 30 seconds. This is the active policy and is enforced by the client implementation and its contract test.

## Migration history

The client previously used a 10-second timeout. That value has been superseded by 30 seconds; references to 10 seconds describe only the former policy and must not be presented as current behavior.

## Consequences

The architecture page, implementation, and tests now agree on the 30-second timeout. The former 10-second value remains identifiable as history without appearing to be current behavior. Update the architecture page and this decision note whenever the policy changes.
